Lucy Hale stood by the newel, hands clasped so tight the knuckles showed white; she was plainspoken in her grief and in her fear — inheritance anxiety, you could call it, though that is a small thing when a man is dead.
Lucy answered in short, trembling sentences. She could not hide how thin her voice had gone: "I— I was in the drawing-room. I heard the bell. I went to the study when Alfred called."
"I— I was in the drawing-room. I heard the bell. I went to the study when Alfred called."
